What is the essential teaching in '88. Only practice can resolve doubt'?

In '88. Only practice can resolve doubt', the teaching opens with this observation: *"Only practice can resolve doubt]
When people asked Luang Pu about death and rebirth, or about past and future lives, he was never interested in answering."* The central invitation is to turn one's investigation inward — to verify the Dhamma not as a set of beliefs, but as directly observable reality in one's own body, speech, and mind. As the text teaches, the Dhamma is *akāliko* — ever-present — and *opanayiko* — leading inward — available to be known (*paccattaṁ*) by each practitioner for themselves. There is no need to search elsewhere; the truth is already here.
